title: Sex- and age-specific development of ssRNA virus receptor expression in the human brain
summary: Postmortem transcriptomes from 33 donors across 15 brain regions were used to characterize developmental expression trajectories for 67 single-stranded RNA-virus receptor genes. The analysis reported nonlinear, sex-biased trajectories, with roughly half of female–male gene-region trajectory pairs diverging and strongest differences in cortex and early childhood. These are retrospective expression patterns, not evidence of infection susceptibility.
ai_technology: Random Forest classifies case sex from LOESS-derived developmental receptor-expression profiles, supporting the reported structured sex-specific expression patterns.

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: LOESS trajectories and clustering described expression patterns; Random Forest sex classification was evaluated by leave-one-case-out refitting.
evidence.unknown: Small postmortem dataset and exploratory receptor-expression interpretation; no external cohort or infection outcome was tested.
